instruction: Add a 'Max' row below the sales data showing the highest sales value for each month across all reps.

metadata.trajectory_summary: Agent typed 'Total' in A13 (skipping row 12), correctly computed SUM formulas for all 6 months (B13:G13), then attempted to create a chart but produced scatter/points instead of a line chart. Total row values were correct but chart type was wrong.
metadata.capability_extraction: Can type text into cells, use SUM formulas, navigate LibreOffice menus, create charts via Insert menu
metadata.failure_analysis: Model failed because: (1) placed Total in row 13 instead of row 12, (2) created scatter chart instead of line chart, (3) x-axis showed numbers instead of month names. The SUM computation was correct.
metadata.task_rationale: Tests MAX formula capability, a natural variation of the SUM task the model demonstrated. Same pattern (label + formula per column) but different aggregation function.
metadata.explanation: Task requires adding a Max row with MAX formulas for each month (B-G). Getter scans column A for 'Max' label and reads values from that row. Metric compares each column value against expected maximums with 0.5 tolerance. Partial credit: each correct column gives 1/6 of total score.

llm_judge_reasons: Getter correctly scans column A for 'Max' label (case-insensitive) and returns values from columns B-G, matching the instruction's requirement to check max values per month.
Metric correctly handles expected parameter for type='rule' — accesses expected.get('expected_values') and expected.get('tolerance') directly from the rules dict.
Partial credit logic is sound: each of the 6 month columns contributes 1/6 to the total score.
Postconfig correctly activates the window and saves the file (Ctrl+S) before the getter reads, ensuring fresh data on disk.
Complete coverage: all 6 month columns (B-G) are verified, matching the instruction's 'each month' requirement.
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Minor: Expected max values (767, 773, 722, 714, 730, 783) cannot be independently verified without downloading the source XLSX. If these are incorrect, the evaluator would wrongly reject correct solutions.
